display.purpose: Course title in the Syllabus masthead, on the bench; Latin and digits in Rail, CJK in the system sans.

numeral.purpose: Frame numbers in the Syllabus list; scales to clamp(3.25rem, 2.2rem + 3vw, 5rem) at line-height 0.8 beside a Handout or title-slide title.

headline.purpose: Lesson title on a Handout and title slide.

title.purpose: Handout section headings; Syllabus Lesson titles at 1.25rem/1.4; slide headings at 1.6em.

body.purpose: Handout running text in a 48rem column; 1.0625rem/1.85 below 640px.

body-ui.purpose: Default size for everything outside the Handout text.

label.purpose: Rail cells (1rem Handout, 1.25rem Slides, up to 1.6rem Syllabus), slide count, citation markers at 0.62em.

meta.purpose: Topics, frame actions, crumbs, facts, Sources panel (0.875-0.95rem).

shadows.name: source-highlight-bleed
shadows.purpose: Extends a targeted Source highlight past its text box. Not elevation; the system is flat.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The single easing: rail cell hover (0.2s), objectives chevron turn (0.2s), Source arrival flash (1.4s).

motion.name: cited
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: arriving at a Source from a citation. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

constraints: Every page is one offline HTML file that fetches nothing; CSS, script, and the Rail face (data URI) are inlined.
Latin numerals and labels use the embedded Rail face (Barlow Condensed 600, Latin subset, OFL); CJK uses the named system sans stack, never system-ui.
Exercise answers fold in native <details> without script.
Slides read without script (all slides in turn); slides.js adds one-at-a-time presenting.
Dark mode flips only the paper window tokens; the bench and rail stay.

narrative.overview:
A Course is a strip of film laid on an editor's bench. The bench is near-black and owns the frame on every page, in both colour modes. The Lessons run along one perforated orange rail as numbered frames; on Slides the same rail carries the slides. Reading happens only inside paper windows punched into the bench, so the long-form text always sits on a calm, warm surface, never on the dark.

State is a mark, not a hue. A paper-filled frame is where you are (or where you last stopped), an inked frame is one opened before, an outlined frame is not opened yet; a folded tape flag tags the marked frame. Numbers are the system's display voice: frame numbers, citation markers, exercise counters, and the slide count all set in one condensed grotesk, while CJK text falls to the system sans.

The pages are dense but quiet: a 30-Lesson Course fits one rail row at 1440px and a two-column contents list, and a Handout reads at a 48rem measure with generous leading. The world refuses the course-platform card grid and the endless document scroll.
keyCharacteristics: Bench black frames every page in both modes; only the paper windows flip in dark mode.
One perforated orange rail is the navigation on all three page types.
Square everything: no corner radius anywhere a reader can touch.
Flat by default: depth comes from bench, rail, and paper planes, not shadows.
Numerals in the embedded condensed face; CJK in the system sans; no web fetch.

rules.name: The Bench Stays Rule
rules.body: Dark mode dims the paper window and nothing else. The bench and the rail are the same in both modes; the current rail cell is hard-set to light paper (`#f5f1ea` on `#1a1714`) so it still reads as a lit frame on the tape in dark mode.

rules.name: The One Tape Rule
rules.body: Orange is the only hue. On the bench it is `tape`; inside a window it is `tape-deep`. Never introduce a second accent; distinguish states by fill, outline, and flag instead.

rules.name: The Soft Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on a dark surface is a step softer than white (`bench-ink`, dark-mode `ink` `#d6cfc2`), because near-white on near-black glares over a long read.

rules.name: The Edge Number Rule
rules.body: Every numeral that counts or locates (Lesson, slide, exercise, citation, Source marker, Course scope) sets in Rail with tabular figures. Numbers are padded to the width of the largest (`01`–`30`, but `1`–`9`).

rules.name: The No system-ui Rule
rules.body: CJK text never resolves through `system-ui`: on Windows in Chinese it falls back to PMingLiU, a thin serif that tires the eyes. Use the named sans stack. This is a product constraint, not taste.

rules.name: The Embedded Face Rule
rules.body: The only non-system face is Rail, inlined as a data URI so every page renders its numerals offline. Never link a web font or CDN; never extend Rail to CJK.

rules.name: The Three Planes Rule
rules.body: Bench, tape, paper, in that order; never a card floating on paper, never a shadow to lift something. A new surface is either a window (paper), a recess (paper-2 or tint), or a mark on the tape.

rules.name: The Square Frame Rule
rules.body: Nothing a reader touches is rounded. The sprocket hole is the world's own material and the only exception.

dos: **Do** keep bench black (`#0c0b0a`) as the page ground on every page in both modes, and flip only the window tokens in dark mode.
**Do** put every Lesson (or slide) on one perforated rail and mark position with fill and flag: paper = here, bench = seen, outline = not yet.
**Do** set every counting or locating numeral in Rail 600 with tabular figures, padded to the widest number.
**Do** keep running text inside a paper window at a 48rem measure with 1.9 line-height.
**Do** use `tape` on the bench and `tape-deep` inside the window, so orange text clears 4.5:1 on paper.
**Do** fold Exercise answers in native `<details>`, and keep Slides fully readable with script off.
**Do** theme the browser surfaces from the palette: `::selection` in tape, 2px `tape` focus ring at 2px offset, bench scrollbars.
**Do** ship every page as one file that fetches nothing: CSS, script, and the Rail face inlined.
donts: **Don't** use `system-ui` anywhere in a font stack; CJK on Windows would fall to PMingLiU.
**Don't** link a web font, CDN, or any network asset; don't extend Rail beyond Latin and numerals.
**Don't** round corners on windows, cells, buttons, or panels; the sprocket hole is the only curve.
**Don't** add shadows for depth or float cards on the paper; use the three planes.
**Don't** introduce a second accent hue or signal state by colour change alone.
**Don't** set paragraphs, claims, or Sources on the bench; the bench carries titles, facts, crumbs, and navigation only.
**Don't** add a small label above a heading; the heading carries its own weight. The tape strip above a section heading is a mark, not text.
**Don't** turn the Syllabus into a card grid or a single long scroll; it is the rail plus a two-column contents list.
